category_title: Elementary students with ASD and language delay who generalize virtual experiences to real-world social interactions
minimal_context: The student is answering a series of question-based learning items in a virtual zoo environment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start the virtual zoo lesson. Please answer the 12 questions on the screen.

STUDENT: (Answers a few questions, then looks away from the screen, distracted by the kids walking outside the classroom.) How many questions are left?

TUTOR: Just keep going. Listen to the audio description for the next question.

STUDENT: (Listens to the long aural feedback but becomes easily distracted by the extra information, losing attention to the learning task.)

TUTOR: Please look back at the screen. We are on question number seven now.

STUDENT: (Hears the peak sounds of the whale in the virtual zoo and reacts very sensitively to the sound, completely losing attention to the surroundings after having answered 6 questions.)

options.A: Have the student answer the questions by tracing along the screen with their finger during the virtual zoo lesson.
options.B: Provide fewer learning materials and test items embedded in the virtual zoo lesson, limiting the task to no more than six items.
options.C: Instruct the student in knowledge of self-regulation strategies and promote their efficacy for using them during the virtual zoo lesson.
options.D: Provide follow-in talk that is related to the student's ongoing actions and attention during the virtual zoo lesson.
